candidate_replacement.delivery: Rift2Core's build.sc declares Chisel as the compiled Maven artifact org.chipsalliance::chisel:5.1.0, so this definition reaches the CPU as a class file rather than as a file in the CPU source tree. harness/evaluate.sh splices the candidate class into a pristine copy of the pinned file above with ../_shared/replace_class.py, compiles that single file against the same pinned artifact in a throwaway mill module, rewrites the Arbiter class entries of chisel_2.13-5.1.0.jar inside a private copy of the pinned Coursier cache, and builds Rift2Core with COURSIER_CACHE pointed at that copy. The other definitions in the pinned file (ArbiterIO, ArbiterCtrl, LockingArbiterLike, LockingRRArbiter, LockingArbiter, RRArbiter) stay at their pinned revision.

test_programs.policy: Run every program in the fixed required-test catalog that matches the selection patterns.

fixed_test_patches.purpose: Add a CPU_EVAL_OBSERVATION_MISMATCH probe to LsuBase and DcacheBase, outside the chisel3.util.Arbiter class body candidates replace, covering the six live multi-input instantiations Lsu.ls_arb, Lsu.lu_wb_arb, Lsu.irtn_arb, Lsu.frtn_arb, Dcache.op_arb and Dcache.rd_arb. The probe re-derives the arbitration contract from each site's own input valid signals and flags any cycle where the candidate's driven chosen, out.valid or per-input transfer disagrees, comparing only protocol-observable quantities so that the value of ready on an input that is not asserting valid is not constrained. The probe also emits CPU_EVAL_ARBITER_CONTENTION, a per-instance counter capped at eight reports for cycles in which two or more inputs compete. This marker does not affect the verdict.

comparison.pass_condition: Every selected program completes with zero RTL-versus-ISA trace mismatches and no CPU_EVAL_OBSERVATION_MISMATCH marker from harness/observe_arbiter.patch.
